description:
Schloss Saalhof in Maishofen is one of the oldest noble seats in the Pinzgau, according to German Wikipedia, the main source for this chronology; in 1296 it probably belonged to a knight known as "Konrad der Teufel" (Konrad the Devil). The estate was a fief of the archbishops of Salzburg and is first documented in 1423, in the hands of Oswald Eisenstang.

Under Cristoff Amann von Judendorf zu Saal the present manor house was built on older foundations at the start of the 17th century; a marble plaque above the ogee-arched doorway records the completion of the works in 1606, and much of the interior dates from that time. A coat of arms on the first floor records the marriage of Mathias Riedl in 1661, and in 1766 the Salzburg botanist Franz Anton Alexander von Braune was born in the castle.

In 1840 an innkeeper from Weissbach bought it, and the castle has since passed down through the same farming family to the Rieders, who still run the farm. A full renovation began in 2004, and in 2010 the façade was restored to its original 17th-century colours; the castle, the 1686 farm manager's house and a wayside cross have been protected as a listed ensemble since 1992. Since 2006 the owners have let holiday apartments and guest rooms, and today the castle offers holiday apartments with kitchens and a sauna on a working farm between Zell am See and Saalbach.
history: Schloss Saalhof in Maishofen is one of the oldest noble seats of the Pinzgau, probably held in 1296 by a knight called Konrad der Teufel and documented from 1423 as a fief of the archbishops of Salzburg. The present manor house was built on older walls at the start of the 17th century and completed in 1606. It passed through several noble families, and the botanist Franz Anton Alexander von Braune was born there in 1766. In 1840 it was bought by a local innkeeper, and it has since passed down through the same farming family. A renovation from 2004 restored the castle, whose 17th-century façade colours were brought back in 2010, and since 2006 the family has let holiday apartments on the working farm.

faqs.question: How old is Schloss Saalhof?
faqs.answer: The noble seat is recorded from 1296 and documented from 1423; the present manor house was completed in 1606 on older foundations.

faqs.question: Is Schloss Saalhof a hotel?
faqs.answer: It offers self-catering holiday apartments on a working farm run by the family that has owned the castle since 1840; Booking required a minimum stay of four nights on the January dates checked.

meta_title: Saalhof Castle, Maishofen — Castle Holiday Apartments in the Pinzgau
meta_description: Stay at Saalhof Castle in Maishofen near Zell am See, Austria — holiday apartments in a 1606 manor house on a working farm. From approx. €278/night.

hotel.room_location_note: Holiday apartments are in the castle and the buildings of the farm estate; ask the owners which building your apartment is in
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** The castle stands at Saalhofstraße 26 in Maishofen, in the Pinzgau between Zell am See and Saalbach-Hinterglemm, in Salzburg State; Booking notes train access. Booking lists free private parking with electric charging and accessible parking.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €278/night for a 56 m² apartment for two adults with a king bed and a single bed, a private kitchen with a dishwasher, a sauna, a barbecue, a mountain view and free Wi-Fi, with free cancellation on the rate seen; a two-bedroom apartment with a balcony was around €311 a night. Booking required a minimum stay of four nights on the dates checked, and showed taxes and fees of about €103 for the four nights (around €26 a night) separately.

**On-site:** Self-catering apartments, a sauna and massages, a working farm, free parking and free Wi-Fi; Booking lists the property as wheelchair accessible.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for one January 2027 stay, so check your own dates on Booking. This is a self-catering apartment stay on a working farm, not a full-service hotel, and the castle itself is private and not open to visitors.

**Combine with:** [Mittersill Castle](/castles/austria/mittersill-castle), another castle hotel in the Pinzgau, about 25 km to the west.
